_note: Sidecar for the v0.1.20 NCL Aura hosted solo group pack (Miami, Oct 14-21 2028; Puerto Plata, St. Thomas, Tortola, Great Stirrup Cay). Built 2026-10-05 from in-session research: three read-only research passes plus direct checks in the main session. Nothing is inherited from the v0.1.11 Escape sidecar, which covers the same four ports; every port claim here was looked up again. Aura is not yet delivered (first sailing May 2027), so every ship fact is NCL's pre-delivery announcement, and the pack says so. Where only a search-engine snippet of a government page could be read (several .gov sites refused this environment), the entry says [SNIPPET] and the pack either leaves the number out or tells the reader to check it.
verified_by: Claude Code session for operator Ken Baker

weather_normals.method: Open-Meteo historical weather API, daily temperature_2m_max/min and precipitation_sum at each port's coordinates, Oct 14-21, years 2020-2024 (40 days per port), simple mean; wet day = precipitation_sum > 1.0 mm. See values_and_model for which model.

values_and_model.values: Miami 82/72 F, 68% wet; Puerto Plata 87/76, 50%; St. Thomas 84/81, 52%; Tortola 84/81, 48%; Great Stirrup Cay 82/78, 52%
values_and_model.model: Default archive model (ERA5-based). A second run with models=ecmwf_ifs returned byte-identical values and the same grid point.
values_and_model.grid_note: For St. Thomas the API's grid point is 18.3128N, 64.9512W at elevation 0.0, i.e. over water; the pack says so and explains the high night-time lows rather than adjusting the numbers.

cluster_detection.notes: Layer 2: the house template's repeated 'Things to know' sub-heads. Counter-signals: dated first-person boundary, sourced numbers with years, plain refusals to print unsourced figures, and port-specific timing advice (Tortola's 1:00 PM all-aboard, the 10:00 AM downtown St. John ferry).
